headline: Majors hold the 200-day line but momentum has stalled; whales moving coins onto exchanges while funding diverges by asset.
paragraphs: The regime is intact but cooling. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and four of those five (all except XRP) have confirmed golden crosses. Doge and Ada have already fallen below the 200-day line, a split that matters: the top of the market is still in an uptrend structure, but the breadth is narrowing. Bitcoin is down 2.8 percent on the day and 4.8 percent on the week, though up 19.7 percent on the month, the familiar pattern of a rally in rest. Ethereum down 4.4 percent today and 3.1 percent on the week but up 29.4 percent on the month. Solana down 4.2 percent today and 4.9 percent on the week but up 33.6 percent on the month. Every major shows the same tension: weakness intra-week against a strong monthly backdrop. The market cap dropped 6.58 percent over the last 24 hours to 2.6 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance sits at 58.4 percent, neither extreme.

Momentum has neither confirmed the move higher nor inverted it; it is simply neutral. Across the majors, RSI-14 hovers in the 45 to 56 range, with no asset overbought and most in the middle third of the scale. Critically, MACD is below signal for every asset in the list. That means the 12-26-9 oscillator has not yet rolled positive on the current move, a lagging indicator but a real one. Bitcoin's RSI at 49.4 and Ethereum's at 50.8 are textbook neutral, neither momentum nor capitulation. When price is up on the month but MACD sits below signal and RSI is centered, the market is resting inside an uptrend without the juice to push through. Doge and Ada, both below the 200-day line and both with RSI below 46, are the only two showing true momentum weakness, and their monthly gains (15.3 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively) are the smallest in the set.

Derivatives positioning exposes a crowded long. Bitcoin funding on OKX is 0.0052 percent per 8 hours, annualizing to 5.7 percent, meaningfully positive and the market's way of charging longs for holding the position. Open interest stands at 2.1 billion USD, substantial. The long-to-short ratio is 1.78, meaning 78 percent more longs than shorts in the aggregate. Liquidations in the past hour show shorts being cleared ($1.19 million) far more than longs ($387k), a sign that the downside move is shaking out over-leveraged bets on further decline. Ethereum's funding has turned negative at minus 0.23 percent per 8 hours (minus 2.6 percent annualized), a rare inversion; the long-short ratio there is 2.12, even heavier long, and 73.7 million in shorts got liquidated in the last hour against just 73k in longs. Solana and XRP are also seeing negative funding (minus 2.9 and plus 6.1 percent annualized, respectively), but Doge's funding has spiked to 1.0 percent per 8 hours (11 percent annualized), the highest on the board and a signal that leverage is flowing into the weakest momentum asset. The long-short on Doge is 4.78, the most extreme ratio of any asset here.

Whale behavior is sending coins toward the exchanges. Over the last 24 hours, 48.2 million USD in net value moved onto exchanges, with Bitcoin accounting for 76.9 million of that inflow into Binance against zero outflow, a clean entry signal. Over the weekly window, the pattern is more telling: week ending August 25 saw 1.09 billion move onto exchanges, the week of September 1 saw 49 million, September 8 saw 351 million, and the week ending September 15 has already tallied 613 million. That is four consecutive weeks of net inflow, with the most recent the heaviest, even as retail pricing (the Fear and Greed gauge at 69, in Greed territory) stays elevated. Stablecoin float sits at 310.3 billion, up just 1.35 percent on the month, so the dry powder available to deploy is not expanding; what is happening is coins moving to venues where they can be sold or margined.

Spot ETF flows are split. Bitcoin saw an inflow of 159.9 million USD on September 14, but the five-session net is minus 302.8 million, meaning one day of buys cannot erase the earlier week's selling. Only one direction has held for two days, so no persistence yet. Ethereum printed 121.1 million inflow on September 14 and the five-session tally is plus 318 million, a coherent bid that has held for two days. The traditional finance money is fractured: Ethereum is being accumulated into spot products at scale, while Bitcoin is struggling. Cumulative Bitcoin ETF flows since inception are 55.4 billion and Ethereum's are 13.5 billion, both substantial and Bitcoin the larger, but on the recent tape they diverge.

The day's core tension is between a regime that is structurally intact (majors above the 200-day, golden cross in place for most) and positioning that is either saturated (long-to-short at 1.78 to 4.78 depending on asset) or contradictory (Bitcoin funding positive while shorts liquidate, Ethereum funding inverted, Doge funding maxed while its technicals are the worst). Whales are consistently moving coins onto exchanges, and spot ETF demand is splitting between Ethereum (sustained) and Bitcoin (one day only). Watch for a reclaim of the weekly highs (Bitcoin 81,264, Ethereum 2,525) or a decisive break of support at the 50-day moving average as the next regime test. Funding flips and large liquidations in a single direction would also signal a decision point imminent.
